Negative Binomial Regression

Source: R/nbreg.R
nbreg.Rd

Fits a negative binomial (NB2) regression model using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficient vector beta, alternated with Newton-Raphson updates for the dispersion parameter theta. No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

nbreg(formula, data, offset = NULL, control = nbreg_control(), weights = NULL)

Arguments

formula

A formula of the form y ~ x1 + x2 + ....

data

A data frame containing the variables in the formula.

offset

An optional numeric vector of offsets on the log-mean scale. Can also be specified in the formula via offset().

control

A list of control parameters from nbreg_control.

weights

Optional prior weights (all 1 by default).

Value

An object of class "nbreg" with components:

coefficients

Named vector of estimated beta coefficients.

theta

Estimated dispersion parameter theta > 0.

SE_theta

Standard error of log(theta).

loglik

Maximised log-likelihood.

vcov

Variance-covariance matrix of beta (treating theta as known).

fitted.values

Fitted means mu_i.

residuals

Response residuals y - mu.

weights

Prior weights used.

nobs

Number of observations.

df.residual

Residual degrees of freedom.

iter

Number of outer iterations.

converged

Logical; TRUE if converged within maxit.

call

The matched call.

terms

The terms object.

model

The model frame.

Warnings

A warning is issued if the algorithm reaches maxit iterations without converging, or if \(\hat heta\) exceeds \(10^4\), which means the data show essentially no overdispersion (the Poisson limit).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
  summary(fit)
}
